# computesphere_alert (Resource)

Manages an alert resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    computesphere = {
      source  = "computesphere/computesphere"
      version = "~> 1.3"
    }
  }
}

variable "api_token" {
  description = "API token for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "account_id" {
  description = "Account ID for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
}

variable "api_url" {
  description = "API URL for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
  default     = "api.computesphere.com"
}

provider "computesphere" {
  api_token  = var.api_token  # or set COMPUTESPHERE_API_TOKEN env variable
  account_id = var.account_id # or set COMPUTESPHERE_ACCOUNT_ID env variable
  api_url    = var.api_url    # or set COMPUTESPHERE_API_URL env variable
}

resource "computesphere_alert" "example" {
  project_id        = "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890ab"
  environment_id    = "e1f2a3b4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab"
  alert_type        = "cpu"
  severity          = "critical"
  threshold         = 80
  evaluation_period = 5
  active            = true
}

output "alert_id" {
  value = computesphere_alert.example.id
}

output "alert_type" {
  value = computesphere_alert.example.alert_type
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `alert_type` (String) What the rule watches: `cpu`, `memory` or `disk` (a metric of the environment's services over `threshold` percent for the evaluation period), or `job_run_failed`, `job_failing_streak` (`threshold` failed runs in a row) or `job_run_missed` for the environment's scheduled jobs.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment this alert belongs to.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project this alert belongs to.
- `severity` (String) Severity level of the alert.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the alert is active.
- `evaluation_period` (Number) Seconds the metric must stay over the threshold; needed for `cpu`, `memory` and `disk`. Rules evaluate in whole minutes, and values under 120 act as 120 (see `effective_evaluation_period`). The job alert types don't use it.
- `threshold` (Number) Percent for `cpu`, `memory` and `disk` (1 to 100); failed runs in a row for `job_failing_streak` (2 to 10, default 3). `job_run_failed` and `job_run_missed` don't use it. When `alert_type` changes to `job_failing_streak` and this is left out, it's set to 3.

### Read-Only

- `effective_evaluation_period` (Number) The window the rule actually evaluates over, in seconds; 0 for a job alert.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the alert.
- `status` (String) The rule's status as the API reports it, e.g. `inactive`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = computesphere_alert.example
  identity = { id = "a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String)

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = computesphere_alert.example
  id = "a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an alert by its ID
terraform import computesphere_alert.example a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab
```
